blocks.text:
This 19-day trip through five Latin American countries starts in Rio de Janeiro during Carnival and continues to Iguazu Falls, Buenos Aires and Santiago. From there you travel into the high-altitude deserts of the Atacama and Bolivia, to the Uyuni Salt Flats and Lake Titicaca. The final leg is in Peru, taking in Puno, Cusco, Machu Picchu and Lima.

The scenery changes sharply along the way. You go from ocean beaches and a night at the Sambadrome to tropical waterfalls, South American capitals, deserts above 4,000 m, salt flats, historic Andean cities and Peru's Pacific coast. With frequent flights and overland transfers between stops, the itinerary is designed for travellers who want to see as much as possible in 19 days.

## Trip highlights

In Rio, see Carnival at the Sambadrome, go up Sugarloaf and Corcovado, explore the city centre and visit the Christ the Redeemer statue. The next major stop is Iguazu Falls, where the itinerary covers both the Brazilian and Argentine sides.

In Buenos Aires, visit La Boca, San Telmo, Plaza de Mayo, Recoleta and newer parts of the city, followed by an evening tango show with dinner. In Santiago, see the historic centre and modern districts before leaving the cities behind for deserts, volcanoes, lagoons and the high plateau.

Travel via San Pedro de Atacama to the Bolivian border and continue in 4x4 vehicles. The itinerary takes in Laguna Verde, Licancabur volcano, the Dalí Valley, the Polques hot springs, the Sol de Mañana geysers, red Laguna Colorada and colonies of James's flamingos.

From there, continue to the Salar de Uyuni, the largest salt flat on the route, then to La Paz, Tiwanaku and Lake Titicaca with its floating Uros Islands. In Peru, travel from Puno to Cusco and Machu Picchu, and finish in Lima.

provenance.wordAbsenceReason: The Word introduction is a short Carnival overview and the rest is split into day-by-day entries. It has no counterpart for this separate route overview and highlights section covering all five countries.
